record.paper_title: Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics
record.original_question: Given a Riemannian manifold (M, g), is it always possible to choose a symmetric (0,3)-tensor T so that, after introducing T, one obtains a dually flat statistical structure {M, g, ∇, ∇*} on M? If this construction is possible but not unique, how should one describe or classify the resulting class of such dually flat spaces?

evidence.quote: For a given Riemannian manifold (M, g), can we always make the quadruplet {M, g, ∇, ∇*} a dually flat space by introducing a symmetric (0, 3)-tensor T? (See [2], [4] and [10].) If this procedure is not unique, what kind of character does the class of those spaces have?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian manifold. A statistical structure on $(M,g)$ is a quadruple $\{M,g,
abla,
abla^{*}\}$, where $
abla$ and $
abla^{*}$ are torsion-free affine connections on $M$ that are dual with respect to $g$, in the sense that
$$X\,g(Y,Z)=g(
abla_{X}Y,Z)+g(Y,
abla_{X}^{*}Z)$$
for all vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on $M$. Equivalently, given a symmetric $(0,3)$-tensor $T$ on $M$, one defines $
abla$ and $
abla^{*}$ by
$$g(
abla_{X}Y,Z)=g(
abla^{g}_{X}Y,Z)-	frac{1}{2}T(X,Y,Z),\qquad g(
abla^{*}_{X}Y,Z)=g(
abla^{g}_{X}Y,Z)+	frac{1}{2}T(X,Y,Z),$$
where $
abla^{g}$ is the Levi-Civita connection of $g$. The statistical structure $\{M,g,
abla,
abla^{*}\}$ is called dually flat if both $
abla$ and $
abla^{*}$ are flat (i.e., have vanishing curvature).

Address the following two questions:

(a) Does there exist, for every Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$, a symmetric $(0,3)$-tensor $T$ on $M$ such that the resulting quadruple $\{M,g,
abla,
abla^{*}\}$ defined above is a dually flat statistical structure on $M$?

(b) Whenever such a tensor $T$ exists but is not unique, give a description or classification of the family of all dually flat statistical structures $\{M,g,
abla,
abla^{*}\}$ thereby obtained on $(M,g)$.
artifact.category_tag: Information geometry / dually flat statistical structures
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turn up active literature on dually flat structures, Hessian manifolds, and singular/quasi-Hessian extensions, but no source establishes a definitive yes/no answer for the existence of a symmetric (0,3)-tensor T producing a dually flat statistical structure on an arbitrary Riemannian manifold (M,g), nor a complete classification when nonunique. The status of the problem as posed could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: The dually flat structure for singular models
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces quasi-Hessian manifolds with possibly degenerate metric and a symmetric cubic tensor, extending statistical manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues to extend the framework of dually flat statistical structures, indicating the original existence/classification question is not settled in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Information geometry (Japanese Journal of Mathematics survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of information geometry; dually flat structures arise from divergences and Hessian potentials but global existence on arbitrary Riemannian manifolds is not asserted.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of a global dually flat structure on a general (M,g) is not established as a theorem in the surveyed literature.
